cases.title: Verify that a fresh Node process reuses the original payment ID when recovering the same SQLite-backed pay run
cases.preconditions: Node.js 22.13 or later and the execution-project dependencies are installed. PAYROLL_TEST_BUILD_DIR identifies the buggy or fixed application directory. Use the test-created temporary database, not either application's normal database.
cases.data: One approved NGN150,000 earning; persistent temporary SQLite file; notification failure.
steps: From execute_test_cases, run npm run test:service with PAYROLL_TEST_BUILD_DIR pointing to the selected application. The check performs the following steps in an isolated temporary SQLite file.
Create a single workspace and arm one notification failure in PayrollService.
Execute its 13 October pay run and retain the payment ID; confirm NGN 150,000.00 recorded and one pending notification.
Close the first PayrollService connection to the database.
Start a new Node process using the same database file and workspace ID, and execute the original pay run again.
Read the fresh process result and compare recorded pay, payment count, original payment ID and pending notifications.
cases.expected: The fresh process returns exactly one NGN 150,000.00 payment with the original payment ID. Pending notifications become 0. This checks graceful close/reopen recovery.

POST /api/workspaces/{id}/retry-notifications with {}. Do not submit another pay-run request.
Compare the returned payments array with the saved array and inspect pendingNotifications and providerAccepted.
cases.expected: The complete payments array is unchanged. pendingNotifications becomes 0 and providerAccepted is exactly 1.

cases.title: Verify that skip navigation, route focus and the payroll confirmation controls follow the tested keyboard sequence
cases.preconditions: Selected build is running locally: buggy http://127.0.0.1:4175 or fixed http://127.0.0.1:4176. Automation serves the selected build on port 4184. Seeded employees and bank destinations are unchanged. Use fresh workspaces that are not reused by other cases.
cases.data: Overview loaded; keyboard navigation only for the tested sequence.
steps: POST /api/workspaces with {"fixture":"single"}. Confirm HTTP 201 and save the returned id as {id} for every subsequent request.
Open /overview?workspace={id} and wait for Payroll overview.
Press Tab to focus Skip to content, then Enter; check that main receives focus.
Focus Review pay run and press Enter; check that the Pay runs heading receives focus.
Focus Review and process payroll and press Enter; check that Cancel receives focus.
Press Tab once and check that Process payroll receives focus.
Press Escape and check that focus returns to Review and process payroll.
cases.expected: Skip to content focuses main. Activating Review pay run focuses the Pay runs heading. The dialog focuses Cancel first, then Process payroll on Tab. Escape restores focus to Review and process payroll.

cases.preconditions: Selected build is running locally: buggy http://127.0.0.1:4175 or fixed http://127.0.0.1:4176. Automation serves the selected build on port 4184. Seeded employees and bank destinations are unchanged. Use fresh workspaces that are not reused by other cases.
cases.data: Employee Daniel Mensah; masked account ending 3068.
steps: POST /api/workspaces with {"fixture":"single"}. Confirm HTTP 201 and save the returned id as {id} for every subsequent request.
Open /employees?workspace={id} and select Daniel Mensah.
Read the employee heading and masked account destination.

Read the selected Employee value on the earning form.

cases.data: Three employees; approved payroll NGN435,000.
steps: POST /api/workspaces with {"fixture":"standard"}. Confirm HTTP 201 and save the returned id as {id} for every subsequent request.
Open /overview?workspace={id} and wait for the page to load.
Read the page heading and payroll metric values.
Inspect the rendered page text for Acme, MustBank, WebMCP, Quest, assessment, sandbox, fictional and test credits, ignoring case.

cases.title: Verify that retrying a pending notification in the UI preserves the payment and disables recovery after completion
cases.preconditions: Selected build is running locally: buggy http://127.0.0.1:4175 or fixed http://127.0.0.1:4176. Automation serves the selected build on port 4184. Seeded employees and bank destinations are unchanged. Use fresh workspaces that are not reused by other cases.
cases.data: One successful payment with notification failure.
steps: POST /api/workspaces with {"fixture":"single"}. Confirm HTTP 201 and save the returned id as {id} for every subsequent request.
POST /api/workspaces/{id}/faults with {"kind":"notification"} to arm one local, single-use failure.
Send POST /api/workspaces/{id}/run with {"scheduledFor":"2026-10-13T09:00:00.000Z"} and retain the complete original payments array.
Open /notifications?workspace={id} and read the delivery-unavailable message.
Select Retry pending notifications and wait for Notification recovery finished.
Send GET /api/workspaces/{id}; compare complete payment objects and read pendingNotifications.
Check whether Retry pending notifications is disabled.
cases.expected: The complete payments array is unchanged, pendingNotifications is 0 and the successful recovery message is displayed. Retry pending notifications is disabled.

cases.title: Verify that two tabs retain their own workspace and selected pay date after navigation and reload
cases.preconditions: Selected build is running locally: buggy http://127.0.0.1:4175 or fixed http://127.0.0.1:4176. Automation serves the selected build on port 4184. Seeded employees and bank destinations are unchanged. Use fresh workspaces that are not reused by other cases.
cases.data: A selects 20 October; B remains on 13 October.
steps: Create workspace A with fixture single and B with fixture standard; retain their separate IDs.
In tab A, open /overview?workspace={A}, choose pay date 20 October, then navigate to Employees and back to Overview.
Open /overview?workspace={B} in a second tab and read its NGN 435,000.00 metrics.
Reload tab A; read its Pay date and Pending approvals. Change A back to 13 October and read its NGN 150,000.00 metrics.
Reload tab B; read its Pay date and metrics and compare them with A's values.
cases.expected: A retains 20 October and 0 pending approvals after its reload, then shows NGN 150,000.00 when changed back to 13 October. B independently retains 13 October and NGN 435,000.00 after reload.

cases.title: Verify that the served build matches the assessed manifest and rejects a request to switch to the opposite payment implementation
cases.preconditions: Selected build is running locally: buggy http://127.0.0.1:4175 or fixed http://127.0.0.1:4176. Automation serves the selected build on port 4184. Seeded employees and bank destinations are unchanged. Use fresh workspaces that are not reused by other cases.
cases.data:
Expected metadata: execution project results/builds.json.
Buggy app policy-switch request: {"fixture":"single","behavior":"fixed"}.
Fixed app policy-switch request: {"fixture":"single","behavior":"faulty"}.
steps: Read results/builds.json in the execution project and note the selected buildId and sourceFingerprint.
GET /api/health from the selected running application.
Compare health.build.id and health.build.sourceSha256 with the selected entry in results/builds.json.
POST /api/workspaces with {"fixture":"single","behavior":"fixed"} against the buggy app, or behavior faulty against the fixed app.
Record the policy-switch request's HTTP status.
cases.expected: The served build ID and source fingerprint match the selected application's assessed metadata. Attempting to select the opposite implementation returns HTTP 400.
